title: Long-term culture and electrophysiological characterization of human brain organoids
protocol: Recoat a 100 mm tissue culture dish with a 1% Geltrex solution in DMEM/F-12.
Incubate the coated dish at 37°C for at least 30 minutes.
Thaw cells from cryovial in a 37°C water bath.
Transfer thawed cell contents to a 15 mL conical tube containing 4 mL pre-warmed mTeSR.
Centrifuge at 200 g for 4 min, then aspirate supernatant and resuspend pellet in mTeSR with ROCK inhibitor (12.5 μM).
Transfer cells to the coated 100 mm tissue culture dish and incubate at 37°C.
Replenish the medium daily by completely aspirating the mTeSR and replacing it with 10 mL of fresh mTesR.
Passage PSCs when they reach 70% confluency.
Prepare a new 10 cm Geltrex-coated dish as described above.
Aspirate mTeSR from the culture dish and add 5 mL Gentle Cell Dissociation Reagent for a 10 cm dish.
Incubate at room temperature for 5-6 minutes until colonies separate into pieces but not detach completely.
Aspirate reagent, then add 5 mL mTeSR to the cells.
Use a cell lifter to gently scrape off colonies using a circular motion.
Slowly trititate colonies four times using a 5 mL pipette, avoiding single-cell suspension.
Pipette off 2.5 mL of cell aggregates and transfer to a 15 mL conical tube.
Make a 1:4 dilution of aggregate suspension with mTeSR in the conical tube.
Aspirate excess Geltrex solution from the 10 cm coated dish.
Add 10 mL of the diluted cell aggregate suspension onto the new dish.
Dissociate colonies as per passaging protocol steps 1-7 and collect into a 15 mL conical tube for freezing.
Centrifuge at 200 g for 4 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 0.5 mL of ice-cold freezing media (90% mTESR / 10% DMSO by volume) per cryovial.
Immediately pipette cell suspension into pre-chilled cryovials on ice.
Place cryovials in a freezing container and store at -80°C freezer immediately.
Transfer cryovials to liquid nitrogen for long-term storage after 24 hours.
Grow hPSC colonies in a 100 mm dish until 70% confluent.
Aspirate mTeSR medium and wash plate with 3 mL of PBS.
Aspirate off PBS, then add 5 mL of Accutase and place the dish back in the incubator for 10 minutes.
Cells should detach from the plate. Use a pipettor fitted with a P1000 pipette tip to triturate and wash the plate to detach the remaining cells.
Add cell suspension to a 15 mL conical tube with 5 mL pre-warmed mTESR.
Triturate up and down with a P1000 pipette a few times to ensure a single-cell suspension.
Use a hemocytometer to count a sample of the hPSCs.
Centrifuge cells at 200 g for 3 minutes. Aspirate and resuspend cells in 5 mL of embryoid body medium \(EBM).
Add a volume of the single-cell suspension to a tube of 15 mL of EBM so as to create a suspension with 2,500 cells per 150 μL of EBM.
Pipet hPSC suspension into a reservoir.
Using a multichannel pipette, add 150 μL of cell suspension into each well of a low-attachment, round-bottom 96-well plate.
Replenish EB medium every 48 hours by removing 75 μL of EB medium from each well.
Add 150 μL of fresh EBM to each well for replenishment.
Include Rock inhibitor at 50 μM and bFGF at 4 ng/mL in the EBM for the first four days.
Gently agitate the medium to remove debris before changing the media.
Use a multichannel pipette set at 30 μL to pipette up and down for agitation.
Resuspend and change media starting with the first six columns of the 96-well plate.
Transfer EBs from low-attachment, round bottom 96-well plates to intermediate induction medium in flat-bottom 24-well plates on Day 6.
Fill each well of the 24-well plates with 500 μL of IIM for transfer.
Individually transfer each EB using a cut 200 μL pipette tip to avoid disruption.
Add an additional 500 µl of Neural Induction Medium to each well on Day 8.
Thaw Matrigel at 4°C and keep it on ice throughout the procedure.
Make a grid of indents on Parafilm using sterile scissors for shaping Matrigel droplets.
Spray Parafilm with 70% ethanol before placing it in the tissue culture hood.
Stretch a piece of Parafilm over an empty tip tray for 200 µL sized tips.
Push the Parafilm partway into the holes in the tip tray with a gloved finger, creating smooth hemispheres (dimples).
Detach the Parafilm sheet from the empty tip tray and cut it into 4x4 dimple sheets using sterile scissors.
Place one 4x4 dimple Parafilm sheet in each 60 mm tissue culture dish.
Use a cut-tip 200 µL pipette set at 35 μL to transfer tissues individually from the low-attachment, 24-well plate to a Parafilm dimple.
Aspirate most of the medium used for transferring the tissues using an uncut 200 µL pipette, leaving minimal medium around each tissue.
Add 35 μL of thawed Matrigel to each Parafilm dimple.
Gently reposition each tissue in the middle of the Matrigel droplet using a pipette tip immediately after adding the Matrigel.
Place the dish back into a 37°C incubator for 20 minutes to allow the Matrigel droplets to solidify.
Rinse each Parafilm sheet holding the tissues with 5 mL CDM without vitamin A.
Dislodge any Matrigel droplets from the Parafilm sheet using sterile forceps if necessary.
Remove the Parafilm sheet and ensure each tissue is completely enveloped in a Matrigel droplet.
Repeat steps 3-5 for any organoids that failed to be completely embedded.
Place dish with organoids back in incubator.
Continue culturing.
On Day 12, aspirate off the medium from each dish.
Add 5 mL of fresh CDM without vitamin A to each dish.
On Day 14, use a 50 mL pipette to gently transfer tissues to a 125 mL spinner flask.
Fill spinner flask with 80 mL of CDM containing vitamin A.
Transfer up to 40 organoids per spinner flask.
Maintain cultures on a magnetic stirrer set at 35 rpm.
Replenish the medium once every six days by completely aspirating the old medium.
Add fresh CDM with vitamin A.
On Day 30, add freshly-reconstituted brain-derived neurotrophic factor \(BDNF\) to the flask at a concentration of 14 ng/mL.
From this point on, use media containing BDNF for changes every six days.
Remove cap from one arm of the spinner flasks when changing medium to reach an aspirating pipette into the flask.
Avoid removing the main top cap of the spinner flask to prevent contamination.
Use an aspirating pipette to remove any debris that may accumulate around the paddle of the flask periodically.
Check and replace caps if necessary.
Periodically replace the spinner flasks as needed.
Transfer one organoid from the spinning bioreactor into a 60 mm cell culture dish containing 5 mL of prewarmed Worthington papain solution with 250 μL of Worthington DNase solution.
Cut the organoid into small pieces with a blade.
Place the 60 mm dish that contains the tissue onto a digital rocker in a primary cell culture incubator, and incubate with rocking speed set at 27 rpm for 60 minutes at 37°C.
Collect digested tissues into a 15 mL tube and add 5 mL of RT EBSS.
Triturate the mixture with 10 mL plastic pipette 20 times by pipetting up and down.
Carefully transfer the cloudy cell suspension to a 15 mL tube, avoiding any pieces of undissociated tissue.
Add 2.7 mL of EBSS, 3 mL of reconstituted Worthington inhibitor solution, and 250 µL DNAse solution to the 15 mL tube with the tissue.
Mix gently, avoiding bubbles.
Pellet cells by centrifuging at 300 g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of ice cold neurobasal medium, and filter through a 20 μm Nitex mesh.
Count cells using trypan blue.
Dilute cells in ice cold DPBS+ 0.2% BSA to a concentration of 100 cells/μL.
Place cells on ice until ready for droplet collection.
Assemble a dark box inside the Faraday cage.
Mount the silicon probe and wire up the SmartBox system.
Detach the floating micro-electrode array from its leads.
Make holes in the side of the PTFE teflon tube.
Fix the tissue culture dish to the glass slide using Kwik-Sil.
Mount the PTFE Teflon tube inside the culture dish using Kwik-Sil.
Fix stainless steel disks to the heating stage isolator.
Mount detached floating micro-electrode array inside the inner chamber.
Make one large central hole with Ø 27 mm in the culture dish lid.
Make four small radial holes with Ø 3 mm in the culture dish lid.
Assemble and position carbogen manifold inside the darkbox.
Assemble the organoid chute.
Assemble and collimate the light source.
Position the light source over the recording chamber, centering it on the organoid anchor.
Calibrate LED power using a power meter and sensor in the dark.
Position micro-manipulator and set approach angle for silicon probes at 3-4 mm above the center of the recording chamber's anchor.
Ensure approach angle does not obscure the light path.
Position microscope #1 above the longpass dichroic mirror.
Position microscope #2 close to the recording chamber.
Wire up and ground the DAQ according to the user manual.
Set sampling rate to 30 kHz.
Set DSP cutoff frequency to 1.00 Hz.
Set lower bandwidth to 0.1 Hz.
Set upper bandwidth to 7.5 kHz.
Confirm all analog channels are active.
Confirm digital channels receiving TTL pulses are active.
Prepare aCSF and bubble with 95%O2/5%CO2.
Warm aCSF to 30°C in a water bath.
Position the recording chamber lid.
Position the bath thermistor, carbogen line, and AgCl ground/ref into the outer chamber of the organoid bath.
Turn on the heating stage.
Add 15 mL of aCSF to the recording chamber, maintaining the recording bath at 30°C.
Transfer the organoid from the culture media into a tube with prewarmed aCSF bubbled with 95%O2/5%CO2 in the culture room.
Move the organoid chute into position over the organoid anchor, and lower it into place.
Turn off the room lights, and put on the night vision goggles.
Use a pipette to gently drop the organoid down the chute.
Pipette a few drops of aCSF down the tissue chute.
Let the organoid acclimatize for 30 minutes at 30°C.
Slowly raise the temperature of the recording chamber to 36°C over 30 minutes.
Position the silicon probe over the recording chamber.
Connect the recording chamber AgCl ground/ref to the headstage.
Seal the dark box and turn on the room lights.
Submerge the silicon probe into the aCSF.
Measure the probe impedance at 1000 Hz in aCSF.
View the organoid and silicon probe tip on IR digital microscope #2.
Position the probe tip over the organoid using the three orthogonal axes (x, y, z) of the micro-manipulator.
Zero the axes distance counter on the micro-manipulator controller.
Implant the probe into the organoid.
Monitor the distance advanced along the approach axis using the micro-manipulator controller.
Adjust the probe position until spikes are isolated.
Acquire spontaneous activity.
Trigger light stimulus by sending TTL pulses to the LED driver.
Generate a probe map for the recording setup.
Identify the probe channels with either high or low impedance.
Remove defective probe sites from the list of channels to be analyzed.
Process the raw data file(s) using spike detection and clustering software designed for high density microelectrode arrays.
